questions.stem: A 3-month-old with recent viral symptoms has tachypnea and poor feeding. Which finding should prompt urgent cardiac evaluation even if oxygen saturation is normal?
questions.rationale: Persistent disproportionate tachycardia plus hepatomegaly strongly suggests cardiac dysfunction and can precede hypoxemia.

option_explanations.A: Correct. This combination is a high-yield warning pattern.

questions.board_pearl: Normal oxygen saturation does not rule out heart failure or low cardiac output.

questions.stem: A 12-year-old with suspected myocarditis has mild LV dysfunction. Which test is best for serial bedside assessment of ventricular systolic function during hospitalization?
questions.rationale: Echocardiography is practical and noninvasive for serial assessment of ventricular function and hemodynamic consequences.

option_explanations.A: Correct. It is well suited to repeated bedside functional assessment.
option_explanations.B: Invasive and not appropriate for serial routine monitoring.
option_explanations.D: Not the standard serial functional tool.

questions.board_pearl: Use echo to trend pump function; use CMR to answer tissue-characterization questions.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old has exertional syncope and ventricular arrhythmias. CMR shows extensive fibrofatty replacement of the right ventricle without edema, and there is a family history of sudden death. Which diagnosis is more likely than acute myocarditis?
questions.rationale: Familial sudden death, chronic arrhythmic presentation, and fibrofatty RV disease without acute inflammatory edema point toward arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.

option_explanations.A: Correct. The phenotype is inherited/chronic rather than acute inflammatory.
option_explanations.B: Myocarditis can cause arrhythmia but the imaging and family history point elsewhere.
option_explanations.C: Age and cardiac findings do not fit.
option_explanations.D: Does not explain the structural RV phenotype.
option_explanations.E: Does not fit age or imaging.

questions.board_pearl: A myocarditis-like arrhythmia presentation can unmask genetic cardiomyopathy; family history and tissue pattern matter.

questions.stem: An 8-year-old with myocarditis is hemodynamically stable but has moderate LV dysfunction. Which activity recommendation is most appropriate during the acute phase?

options.E: No activity restrictions are needed if blood pressure is normal

questions.rationale: Exercise is restricted during active myocarditis because of electrical and myocardial risk, even when the child is not in shock.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Activity restriction is part of acute management.
option_explanations.D: Exercise does not treat myocardial injury.
option_explanations.E: Blood pressure alone does not determine exercise safety.

questions.board_pearl: Hemodynamic stability does not equal exercise safety during active myocarditis.

questions.stem: A 5-year-old with suspected myocarditis has hypotension, cool extremities, delayed capillary refill, pulmonary edema, and severe LV dysfunction. Which mistake is most likely to worsen the physiology?

options.A: Repeated large rapid fluid boluses without reassessing congestion
options.E: Transfer planning to an advanced cardiac center

questions.rationale: Excessive volume loading can worsen pulmonary edema and ventricular filling pressures in cardiogenic shock.

option_explanations.A: Correct. This is a major management trap.
option_explanations.E: Appropriate when severe disease may exceed local resources.

questions.board_pearl: The wrong fluid strategy can convert compensated pump failure into overt pulmonary edema.

questions.stem: A 14-year-old with myocarditis develops palpitations and near-syncope. Telemetry shows polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. What is the most important interpretation?

options.A: This represents a potentially life-threatening complication requiring urgent escalation
options.B: This is an expected benign rhythm in teenagers
options.D: The rhythm can be ignored if EF is normal
options.E: It proves the myocarditis has resolved

questions.rationale: Ventricular tachyarrhythmias are among the most dangerous complications of myocarditis and can lead to sudden cardiac arrest.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Electrical instability demands urgent management.
option_explanations.C: It indicates myocardial electrical involvement, not isolated pericarditis.
option_explanations.D: Normal EF does not eliminate arrhythmic risk.
option_explanations.E: It indicates ongoing risk, not resolution.

questions.board_pearl: Normal systolic function does not make malignant ventricular arrhythmia safe.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old with myocarditis is found to have an active infection for which a specific antiviral therapy is clinically indicated. Which principle is most appropriate?

options.A: Treat the identified active infection while continuing supportive cardiac management
options.B: Ignore the infection because all myocarditis treatment is identical
options.C: Stop cardiac monitoring once antiviral therapy starts
options.D: Assume antiviral therapy reverses shock immediately
options.E: Delay stabilization until pathogen confirmation is repeated

questions.rationale: When an active, treatable infection is identified, targeted therapy may be appropriate in addition to—not instead of—supportive management of heart failure, arrhythmia, or shock.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Etiology-specific treatment complements physiologic support.
option_explanations.D: Targeted therapy does not replace acute hemodynamic support.

questions.board_pearl: Treat cause when actionable, but never neglect the physiology.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old with fulminant myocarditis is on VA-ECMO. Which outcome is clinically plausible and should be part of family counseling?

options.A: Recovery of native ventricular function sufficient to wean support
options.D: All survivors have permanent severe cardiomyopathy
options.E: Mechanical support eliminates all arrhythmia risk

questions.rationale: One major purpose of temporary mechanical support in fulminant myocarditis is to bridge the patient through the acute phase to native myocardial recovery when possible.

option_explanations.B: Some patients need transplant, but not all.

questions.board_pearl: Temporary support can buy time for a stunned/inflamed myocardium to recover.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old is 4 months out from myocarditis. He is asymptomatic with normal EF and no arrhythmias on ambulatory monitoring, but inflammatory markers and troponin have not fully normalized. What is the best approach to competitive sports?

options.A: Continue restriction and reassess rather than clear solely on symptoms and EF
options.B: Clear immediately because EF is normal
options.C: Clear if resting heart rate is normal
options.E: Ignore laboratory evidence of ongoing injury

questions.rationale: Return-to-play requires evidence that active myocardial injury/inflammation has resolved in addition to functional and rhythm recovery.

option_explanations.A: Correct. Recovery criteria are not met completely.
option_explanations.D: Competition is not safer than practice.

questions.board_pearl: Do not clear an athlete while evidence of active myocardial injury persists.

questions.stem: A 9-year-old had a viral illness 1 week ago and now has abdominal pain, tachycardia, hepatomegaly, cool extremities, elevated troponin, frequent ventricular ectopy, and depressed biventricular function. Which single statement best summarizes the immediate clinical priority?

options.A: Treat this as high-risk myocarditis with combined pump and electrical instability requiring monitored intensive care and readiness to escalate support
options.B: Focus only on identifying the exact virus before treatment
options.D: Discharge if oxygen saturation is normal

questions.rationale: The child has multiple high-risk domains: low output, congestion, myocardial injury, arrhythmia, and biventricular dysfunction. Stabilization, monitoring, and escalation readiness take precedence over etiologic refinement.

option_explanations.A: Correct. It integrates the full syndrome and prioritizes immediate risk.
option_explanations.B: Etiologic testing must not delay stabilization.
option_explanations.C: Abdominal pain can be a heart-failure presentation and should not distract from the cardiac findings.
option_explanations.D: Normal oxygen saturation does not make this safe for discharge.
option_explanations.E: Exercise testing is inappropriate during active high-risk myocarditis.

questions.board_pearl: The sickest myocarditis cases are recognized by convergence of perfusion, congestion, function, and rhythm abnormalities—not by one laboratory value.
